assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors fuse a deaminase to a Cas9 nickase to make precise C-to-T and A-to-G changes without double-strand breaks or donor templates. This is a clear case of molecular design converting a biological tool into a chemically defined editing reagent, and it is already in clinical use for sickle cell disease and cardiovascular targets. It changes what researchers and clinicians can actually do.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering program; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, including the evolved TadA deaminase) are the first authors of the two decisive papers. Kondo and Nishida independently reported Target-AID with a different architecture and could be an alternative configuration. A Liu-Komor-Gaudelli trio is the most natural, but the committee may prefer Liu alone given that Liu also leads the related prime editing candidate.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across hundreds of labs, crops, animal models and human trials; the first approved base-edited therapies are near or in clinical use. Timing is good, though the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the genome-editing field one the committee may regard as already honored.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees base editing as a distinct chemical advance or an extension of the CRISPR prize.
Overlap with the separate prime editing candidate (B011) and with Liu's directed-evolution work; a combined Liu citation could be needed.
Whether Kondo and Nishida deserve inclusion; I cannot independently verify priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade proteins with heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues opens previously undruggable targets and is a genuinely new pharmacological modality. The design principle, a bifunctional molecule that recruits an E3 ligase to a target, is the kind of precise control over molecular recognition I value, and the field has spread rapidly through biomedicine. Cereblon as the target of thalidomide-class glues adds a mechanistic discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the PROTAC concept (Sakamoto, Kim, Crews, Deshaies, 2001); Crews founded the clinical translation. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, underpinning molecular glue degraders. Ciulli and Gray made decisive later contributions (VHL-based PROTACs, structural work), so credit is crowded and the proposed trio omits several defensible people.
assessment.maturity: Multiple degraders are in late-stage clinical trials, with the first approvals still pending to my knowledge. Mechanistic confirmation is strong, but clinical validation is not complete, so timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical proof of benefit is still maturing.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto is contested.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized as one discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery technology that enabled siRNA drugs and the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines. This is a chemical and formulation solution to a core barrier, getting nucleic acids across membranes and out of endosomes, and its societal impact is enormous. As a nanomaterials and biomedicine-oriented member I weigh this very heavily.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Madden and Hope developed the lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid delivery systems and the scalable formulation methods; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan contributed lipid design and siRNA formulation. The 2023 Medicine prize honored mRNA modification, not delivery, so delivery remains unrecognized, but allocating credit among the six names is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale (Onpattro, billions of vaccine doses), with independent confirmation. Recognition is timely. The question is chemistry versus medicine framing.
uncertainties: Division of credit between Cullis's group and the Langer/Anderson and MacLachlan lines.
Possible view that the 2023 Medicine prize already covered the area.
Specific priority claims on ionizable lipids are beyond what I can verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators and clonal clusters made genome sequencing routine and cheap, reshaping biology and clinical diagnostics. The key advance is chemical: reversible terminator nucleotides, fluorescent labeling and surface chemistry. Few analytical methods have changed medicine so broadly.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis approach; Mayer contributed to the clonal-array concept and the Manteia technology. Ju contributed reversible terminator chemistry and Rothberg pyrosequencing-based 454 sequencing, so the credit is shared across technologies; the trio is my best-supported configuration, but a fair prize configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally confirmed, with decades of impact. Timing is arguably late rather than early, which makes it a safe maturity choice.
uncertainties: Disputed allocation across Solexa, 454 and other platforms.
Mayer's role relative to other contributors is uncertain to me.
Whether the committee regards this as chemistry or biology and medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read out enzyme function in native proteomes, and it enabled discovery of new druggable enzymes and covalent ligand screening. This is a chemical-biology method that links chemical reactivity to biological function directly, and it supports drug discovery and chemoproteomics broadly.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt developed the fluorophosphonate-based proteome-wide approach and later chemoproteomics; Bogyo contributed probes for cysteine proteases and in vivo imaging. Overkleeft and Weerapana contributed probes and cysteine reactivity profiling, so a two-person recognition leaves other credible contributors out.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for 25 years with strong independent validation and clinical-stage drugs arising from the platform. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether Cravatt alone is enough versus a shared prize with Bogyo.
Priority claims from early activity-based probe work, which I cannot verify.
Possible overlap with Shokat's covalent drug discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pairs lets cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids in proteins. It offers precise molecular control over protein chemistry and has spread to protein engineering, imaging, biologics and therapeutics, a strong fit for chemical biology and bioorthogonal chemistry, which the 2022 prize recognized in a related form.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the concept and first demonstrations in E. coli, yeast and mammalian cells; Chin extended it to multiple codons, quadruplet codons and animals; Wang contributed early mammalian and in vivo work. Mehl and Yokoyama made substantial contributions, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Long-standing and extensively reproduced, with applications in clinical antibody-drug conjugates. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The relationship to the 2022 click and bioorthogonal prize may reduce novelty.
Credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama.
I cannot verify specific priority timelines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of nanoparticles and spherical nucleic acids connect sequence-specific biomolecular recognition with nanomaterial design. They underpin colorimetric detection, intracellular gene regulation and programmable materials. This is close to my own gold-nanoparticle peptide and biosensing work, and I judge it a conceptually clear design principle with real diagnostics and therapeutics uses.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently reported DNA-directed nanoparticle assembly in 1996; Mirkin developed the spherical nucleic acid concept and its diagnostics and therapeutics applications. Storhoff and Mucic are early coauthors. A Mirkin-Alivisatos pairing is plausible, but Alivisatos's work is distinct enough that the committee may prefer Mirkin alone.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, with commercial diagnostic products and clinical trials. The therapeutic impact is still developing, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Whether spherical nucleic acids and DNA-programmed assembly should be a single discovery.
Therapeutic benefit is not yet clearly established.
The committee recognized quantum dots in 2023, which may reduce the appetite for another nanoscience prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleic acid sequences electrically through nanopores underlies long-read sequencing, with real-time, portable and direct RNA and modification detection. The chemistry of pore engineering and motor proteins is crucial. It changed what researchers and clinicians can do in the field, such as outbreak surveillance.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton, and Akeson proposed and demonstrated single-strand DNA translocation through nanopores; Kasianowicz demonstrated the first single-molecule detection in alpha-hemolysin. Bayley's pore engineering was essential. Credit is spread across at least five contributors, and a three-person set requires excluding at least two defensible names.
assessment.maturity: The technology is commercial and widely validated, with independent platforms confirming the principle. Recognition is timely, though a lot of the key engineering work was done in industry.
uncertainties: Allocation among Deamer, Branton, Akeson, Kasianowicz and Bayley is difficult.
How much of the decisive advance was done in industry rather than academia.
Whether the committee treats this as chemistry.
